chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Rifa'a, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
that he said regarding the sheep: if it blinks its eye or moves its tail, then it is lawfully slaughtered.

key_terms.ذَكِيَّة: Tadhkiya — the state of an animal that has been lawfully slaughtered according to Islamic rites; from the root dhakā, meaning to be pure or sharp
key_terms.طَرَفَتْ عَيْنَهَا: Blinking of the eye — one of the signs indicating the animal was alive at the time of slaughter

ai.seo_question: What are the signs that a sheep was properly slaughtered according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) provides a ruling on verifying that an animal slaughtered for food is properly dead (tadhkiya — the state of being lawfully slaughtered). If a sheep shows signs of life after the slaughter — blinking its eye or moving its tail — it confirms the animal was still alive when the blade passed over the neck, validating the slaughter. This ruling addresses the concern that the animal might have been dead before the knife was applied, which would render it unlawful (haram) to consume.
